scope: 48 selected mechanism comparisons across 16 pinned repositories; not a full audit of every file or a universal market census.

rows.mechanism: Separate active, waiting, someday, completed commitments; preserve waiting-since and due context.
rows.assessment: Existing owner/status/dependency/completion requirements cover the portable mechanism. Mandatory TASKS.md, copied dashboard, weekly deletion and repeated add confirmation are product-specific costs, not missing capability.

rows.mechanism: Resolve aliases progressively from known summary to deeper relevant records; promote frequent context and demote stale entries.
rows.assessment: Existing continuity preserves relevant context with conditional deeper retrieval. A fixed hot-30 directory/profile system is not justified. Unknown alias search falls under scope/terminology recovery; exact organizational decoder is domain data.

rows.mechanism: Compare current local commitments with assigned external items, show additions/completions/staleness, preserve source links.
rows.assessment: Material-change and actual-completion reconciliation already apply. Use stable identity over the source's fuzzy-title-only matching; no universal scan or new tracker. A full synchronization product is outside generic PM ownership.

rows.mechanism: Decompose question into entities, intent, constraints and negations; use tool-supported syntax and aliases; rank by question-specific evidence need.
rows.assessment: Baseline has missing-facts, native source, terminology/scope, authority/conflicts and coverage recovery. No explicit query-planning worked recipe; forward trace Q1 passes without one. Do not adopt all-connected-source fanout, invented numeric relevance weights, or automatic removal of user dates.

rows.mechanism: Merge duplicate reports, retain unique facts, preserve conflicting conclusions and evolving decisions, cite claim provenance.
rows.assessment: Baseline explicitly says duplicates do not add confidence, resolves governing status/applicability, preserves disagreement, and leads with answer. No gap; chronological freshness alone is weaker than baseline supersession rules.

rows.mechanism: Discover relevant available tools, preserve source health and rate-limit coverage, continue useful accessible sources.
rows.assessment: Baseline distinguishes errors/denial from negative findings, reports inaccessible coverage, avoids repeated unchanged attempts and respects actual tool semantics. Tool-prefix existence alone does not establish access; do not import it.

rows.mechanism: Compute available work from people/skills, commitments, absences and overhead; compare demand by role/time and expose bottlenecks/scenarios.
rows.assessment: Existing material capacity/deadline change rule covers decision. A compact conditional arithmetic recipe could make capacity analysis more reproducible, but C1 baseline passes. Fixed 75-80%/50-60% utilization and monthly review are unsupported defaults.

rows.mechanism: Assess affected people/systems/processes; state implementation ownership, recovery trigger/steps and recovery verification.
rows.assessment: SWE already provides more concrete actual recovery/compatibility/verification procedures. Organizational training/adoption details are conditional content for requested change plans, not a new universal PM gate. Do not import automatic ITSM creation/chat posting.

rows.mechanism: Map steps, decisions, handoffs and waits; identify queues/rework/over-processing; compare future state and total outcome costs.
rows.assessment: Baseline requires friction evidence, smallest remedy, total overhead, contrasting cases and maintaining owner. A named waste checklist alone does not establish a missing capability. No routine map or impact measurement mandated.

rows.mechanism: Use before/after changes, dependencies and need-by constraints; account for capacity and affected commitments without false distant precision.
rows.assessment: Scope/outcome tradeoffs, evidence-weighted priority, actual capacity and provisional roadmap commitments are covered. User's genuine added spare capacity need not force a cut; no universal RICE/ICE ratios, cadence or status database.

rows.mechanism: Account for availability and carryover, choose coherent goal, distinguish mandatory and stretch scope, identify dependencies.
rows.assessment: Ready end-to-end slice, acceptance and sequencing already covered. Shares optional capacity recipe with operations; do not add another sprint framework, signoff gate or 70-80% buffer.

rows.mechanism: Extract atomic observations by participant/context, code and group themes, count independent participants, inspect contradictory segments, link findings to evidence.
rows.assessment: Baseline covers behavior/report/inference, contrary cases, duplicates/denominators, population and missingness but has no explicit coding/theme-review recipe. R1 passes with current suite; optional research-synthesis reference is a candidate, not demonstrated failure. Do not impose 5-8 themes, personas, outreach or dashboards.

rows.mechanism: Separate actionable CI/review work from human approval, draft and merge gates; bounded repair/recheck loop with a final feedback refresh.
rows.assessment: Current review has revision-bounded repeated review and delivery has required-check semantics, but no explicit repair-CI feedback convergence procedure. Add optional reference only for a requested repeated repair loop; no demonstrated inability in frozen task.
rows.boundary: Single read-only review; one local known failing test; no requested loop; no tools or authority for remote work. No gh/uv requirement, arbitrary bot allowlist, auto-comments or fixed sleeps.

rows.mechanism: Resolve actual run/job identity and fetch specific failure evidence; distinguish pending logs from unavailable logs.
rows.assessment: Identity, diagnostics and failure classification already present. Specific CI log run/job fallback is a useful example in D01, not independent broad skill expansion.
rows.boundary: No CI failure; existing exact-run diagnostics already sufficient. Do not import source's mandatory approval or provider exclusion.

rows.mechanism: Review full comparison, read surrounding callers and test whether each concern is already handled.
rows.assessment: Destination is stronger: stable snapshot, causal reachability, unsupported unknowns and no finding quota.
rows.boundary: Do not import every-checklist-item-for-every-file ceremony.

rows.mechanism: Review performance by plausible work growth, N+1 queries and unintended allocations.
rows.assessment: Construction structural cost plus performance workload/profile/control guidance already exceed source checklist specificity.
rows.boundary: No mandatory benchmark for evident bounded edits and no measured claim from structural reasoning.

rows.mechanism: Verify feedback root cause and search related call sites before patching.
rows.assessment: Destination has calibrated positive example, semantic variants, path exclusions and scope authority; preserve rather than copying fix-all-instances directive.
rows.boundary: No whole-repository sweep for a local fix.

rows.mechanism: Coherent independently reviewable commits, inspected full branch diff and refreshed reviewer-facing net behavior.
rows.assessment: Commit ownership and publication authority already covered. Optional PR handoff note in D01 can explain whole-current-diff title/body and preserve repository template/current PR state.
rows.boundary: Do not mandate conventional commits, new branch on every task, draft creation, stage-all, dependency installation, pull-from-master or PR creation.

rows.mechanism: Inspect conversation comments, reviews and review threads, respecting pagination and preserving resolved/outdated state.
rows.assessment: Review semantic treatment already covered. D01 can name these distinct feedback surfaces so one endpoint is not claimed as all feedback.
rows.boundary: No need to reread unchanged resolved discussion or import reply/resolve permissions.

rows.mechanism: Own test-server lifecycle, await readiness and clean up owned processes.
rows.assessment: Destination explicitly handles drained pipes, descendants, real readiness identity and exit status; source checks port only, leaves pipes undrained and terminates shell process. Do not transplant helper.
rows.boundary: Use current supported process tool; no new Python/Playwright runner or universal networkidle waits.

rows.mechanism: Observe rendered page before selecting actions; test behavior rather than screenshot presence.
rows.assessment: Current verified artifact identity and client/browser tooling are sufficient; generic always-networkidle advice is not portable to long-polling apps.
rows.boundary: CLI/library tasks have no browser prerequisite.

rows.mechanism: Actionable errors, bounded filtered/paginated outputs, structured schemas and consumer-oriented tools.
rows.assessment: Backend already specifies categories, retry semantics, uncertain outcomes and pagination contracts. MCP-specific schema/annotations should remain platform-specific.
rows.boundary: Do not require MCP stack, exhaustive endpoint coverage or arbitrary default page sizes in all services.

rows.mechanism: Evaluate realistic multi-tool tasks with independently verified stable answers.
rows.assessment: Claim-specific oracles, real consumer paths and evidence layers already covered. Source illustrates valuable task-level tool usability; no need for exactly ten string-match questions or paid evaluations.
rows.boundary: No model evaluation or live data access authorized.

rows.mechanism: Run applicable final gates after stable fixes while reusing focused checks and avoiding setup reruns.
rows.assessment: Destination already conditions reuse on coverage/freshness; SDK strict stack/review order is repo policy, not universal guidance.
rows.boundary: Do not import make/uv, full-stack rerun after every fix, host locks, independent reviewers or sandbox marker exclusions.

rows.mechanism: Docs publication timing must match the available release, separately from preparing documentation.
rows.assessment: Destination covers version-specific examples and safe publication but not whether auto-published live docs describe an unreleased feature. Generic same-change wording can be misapplied. No observed baseline failure is claimed.
rows.boundary: Editorial docs, already released correction, versioned release docs, unpublished internal draft. Do not impose SDK's English-only policy or documentation-nonblocking release rule.

rows.mechanism: Read completed example logs for meaningful actions, reconcile per-item identities and classify skips/errors.
rows.assessment: Destination already rejects green-by-exit-only and skipped-as-pass; scoped log reconciliation is a useful application, not missing doctrine.
rows.boundary: No import of SDK manual-only examples execution prohibition or exact footer schema.

rows.mechanism: Independent released compatibility determination and release metadata must agree.
rows.assessment: Release/package identity and compatibility already covered. Explicit semver bump judgment could help package releases but cannot import SDK pre-1.0 policy. Parent should inspect evolution coverage before deciding.
rows.boundary: No universal patch/minor rules, automatic release tags, complete re-review after irrelevant metadata change, or assumption all CI passed.

rows.mechanism: Share one changeset validation rule source across local review and CI; summaries describe whole branch outcome.
rows.assessment: Single-source ownership and current-net-change principles suffice; source command gathering helper is a concrete implementation for that repo.
rows.boundary: No universal one-changeset rule, LLM CI service, schema or package manager.

rows.mechanism: Calibrate a search against the known defective instance, vary one structural element at a time, then validate each candidate's data flow and guards.
rows.assessment: Calibrated variant analysis already exists in software-debugging/references/investigation-patterns.md. Add a concise local procedure to security/change-review so independently installed security can use it without requiring debugging. This is not a new suite capability.
rows.boundary: No known root cause or no requested broader search: normal review scope. Empty result from an uncalibrated search is not absence evidence. No global repository sweep, fixed false-positive threshold, compulsory query tool or CI rule.

rows.mechanism: Bind secure-erasure claims to actual optimized build evidence and trace secret copies and error exits.
rows.assessment: Secrets row covers injection/storage, lifetime and built output/logs. It does not distinguish source-level wiping from compiler-preserved erasure or copies in memory.
rows.boundary: Only when the requested threat model requires in-memory erasure. No blanket zeroization of ordinary managed-runtime application data; do not claim all copies erased or require nightly tools globally. Retain exact specialist source for an explicit secure-erasure task; no compiler-level verification was executed and no complete zeroization workflow is claimed.

rows.mechanism: Restate trigger/root cause/impact, trace all guards, and try to refute each finding.
rows.assessment: Findings are independently checked against current source; explicit disproof, caller guarantees and meaningful impact already required.
rows.boundary: Do not import mandatory phases, binary verdicts for unresolved facts, module-count routing or agent ceremony.

rows.mechanism: Probe zero/empty/null defaults, dangerous setting combinations and security-relevant API misuse.
rows.assessment: Security error/failure properties, config defaults in change-review and typed runtime validation in backend/construction cover core risk.
rows.boundary: A configurable primitive is not automatically exploitable; establish caller and reachable effect.

rows.mechanism: Follow a protected record across derived copies, deletion/revocation, queued processing and restore; distinguish current authority from historical snapshot.
rows.assessment: Current restrictions across historical recovery explicitly covers later deletions/revocations, derived copies and replay; pipeline and backend references cover ordering and resurrection risks.
rows.boundary: Do not promise instant backup deletion, invent a ledger or elevate unspecified retention preference to vulnerability.

rows.mechanism: Reconstruct strongest controls; separate source-confirmed, unresolved external facts and rejected hypotheses; zero findings is valid.
rows.assessment: Explicit observed/plausible/hardening distinctions, exact blocked boundaries, rejected findings and scope already present.
rows.boundary: Full audit machinery and artifact-promotion protocol are not proportionate defaults for routine changes. Validator prose describes format/consistency, not exploit truth; validator implementations were not re-audited here.

rows.mechanism: Process-wide mutable state can contaminate overlapping server renders; request data must have request lifetime while immutable config and deliberately keyed caches may be shared.
rows.assessment: Narrowest state owner/lifetime plus request/account async ownership and server/browser distinction lead to correct correction in frozen local case.
rows.boundary: Do not ban module scope, immutable config, stateless singleton clients or correctly partitioned caches.

rows.mechanism: Start each independent operation when its actual prerequisites are ready instead of adding a batch-wide barrier.
rows.assessment: Critical path, serialized independent waits, actual ordering dependencies, bounded concurrency and failure/cancellation handling already owned.
rows.boundary: No better-all dependency mandate, universal promise fan-out or inherited 2-10x claim.

rows.mechanism: Separate an error-dominated route from a latency tuning candidate; bind signals to same route/account/window before investigation.
rows.assessment: Workload identity, distributions, errors/timeouts/completed work alongside speed and scope selection already present.
rows.boundary: Helper's 500/1500 ms, 1400/250 invocations, 50% error and confidence .94 are not portable truth. Missing status rows mean no disqualification, not proof of healthy status. No Vercel CLI/account linking or paid observability required.

rows.mechanism: Atomically select and claim a job while letting other workers skip claimed rows.
rows.assessment: Atomic claims, leases/fencing, ack-after-durable-effect, redelivery and failure handling already cover essential correctness beyond the source's claim example.
rows.boundary: Claim success does not recover crashed jobs, enforce fairness or prove exactly-once remote effects. SKIP LOCKED is not a general consistent-view read or mandatory migration approach.

rows.mechanism: Consistent lock ordering reduces deadlocks; inspect blockers and preserve transaction retry semantics.
rows.assessment: Engine/version lock modes, short transactions, blocker/waiter inspection and backend lock order/fresh-read transaction retry present.
rows.boundary: Do not adopt source's implication that a single multirow UPDATE eliminates all deadlocks. Do not treat its example session settings or fixed timeout as universal production recipe.

rows.mechanism: Use authoritative per-principal predicates at data boundary; account for privileged bypass and connection context.
rows.assessment: Explicit pool/scope/context/cleanup/reassignment and privileged bypass procedures are deeper than the small source SET-context example.
rows.boundary: Do not require RLS universally or copy session SET into a pooled service without supported lifetime ownership.

rows.mechanism: Refactor code addresses while preserving managed live-resource identity; inspect actual state and plan replacements.
rows.assessment: Declared configuration vs management mapping vs live resources, compatible versions, ownership, recovery, renames/replacements and safe repair already explicit.
rows.boundary: Do not infer no-change plan proves workload; do not execute init/state mv/apply for research; do not make Terraform mandatory.

rows.mechanism: Acceptance lifecycle includes plan/apply/refresh/final plan/destroy, state checks and import verification; a test is often mutating.
rows.assessment: Static vs plan/mock vs apply verification, resource authorization/bounds/cleanup and live behavior separate from mock success already explicit.
rows.boundary: No default parallel live acceptance tests or sweepers; test naming is not isolation.

rows.mechanism: Distinguish display redaction from secret persistence; ephemeral open/renew/close must match actual credential lifecycle and supported sink.
rows.assessment: State/plan sensitivity and safe handling plus platform secret injection/rotation/lifetime already covered; exact Terraform ephemeral API is specialist implementation knowledge.
rows.boundary: Sensitive label is not evidence of no persistence. Close hook is not evidence of revocation unsupported by issuer. A test echoing secret into inspectable state needs synthetic credentials.

rows.mechanism: Verify review feedback against current contracts and callers before accepting or rejecting it
rows.assessment: Keep supported disproof and independent work. Do not copy blanket stop-for-all-questions, per-item tests or style prohibitions.

rows.mechanism: Check current implementation against accepted intent and unfinished obligations, regardless of task checkmarks
rows.assessment: No mandatory spec scaffold, hooks, append-only backlog or permission to expand beyond the accepted feature.
rows.read_scope: Goal, operating constraints, context, intent inventory, assessment and severity sections.

rows.mechanism: Apply only selected semantic requirement deltas and preserve untouched scenarios
rows.assessment: No CLI/store dependency or source-specific deletion policy. Detect conflicts instead of replacing a conflicting duplicate silently.
rows.read_scope: Setup and selection boundaries, current-spec read, semantic additions/modifications/removals/renames and new-spec handling.

rows.mechanism: Work backward from outcome to substantive artifacts and real wiring; completion claims are not evidence
rows.assessment: Do not import full planning filesystem, universal agent gates, all referenced helper files or automatic human checkpoints.
rows.read_scope: Role, adversarial stance, core principle, context and initial verification/must-have sections. Other helper references not exhaustively audited.

rows.mechanism: Falsify implementation claims and check removed behavior against actual source
rows.assessment: No required reviewer panel or unverified trust in a subagent finding. Existing review already traces deletions, contracts and stale claims.
rows.read_scope: Complete claims-check.md and deletion-check.md; selected step-04-review setup and triage sections.
